business.body:
Olectra Greentech Limited (Hyderabad, incorporated 2000) is one of India's largest manufacturers of electric buses and a maker of composite/silicone polymer insulators. It completed homologation of its first E-Bus in 2017 and has 8+ years of e-bus manufacturing/commercialisation experience. Two reporting segments:
- **E-vehicle division** — electric buses (7m V2, 9m iX, 12m X2, Coach CX2) and electric tippers; the dominant revenue contributor.
- **Insulator division** — silicone/composite polymer insulators (higher-margin niche).

Scale markers (per deck): Market cap ~INR 102.3 bn (~USD 1.2 bn); 2,700+ EVs on Indian roads; 40+ crore (400M+) clean km; 135+ product variants; 1,000+ employees. Manufacturing at a greenfield Hyderabad plant on 150 acres acquired from TSIIC, with initial capacity 5,000 EVs/year scalable to 10,000 EVs/year.

outlook.body:
- Strengthen leadership in India's electric mobility ecosystem through continuous innovation and capacity expansion, backed by disciplined capital allocation
- Expand beyond electric buses into electric trucks and tippers to build a presence across the commercial electric vehicle segment
- Develop an indigenous, in-house electric truck platform whose proprietary architecture and core technology are owned by the Company, with components multi-sourced, to enhance product differentiation and technology ownership

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Olectra operates a state-of-the-art greenfield integrated manufacturing facility in Hyderabad spread over 150 acres, described as India's largest integrated EV manufacturing facility, with an annual production capacity of 2,500 units on a single shift that is scalable to 5,000 units with double-shift operations and a modular layout allowing simultaneous production of multiple vehicle models. During 2025 the Company commenced operations at its Seetharampur state-of-the-art manufacturing facility, strengthening production capabilities; the BRSR penalty disclosure identifies this as the Greenfield EV Manufacturing Facility at Seetharampur Industrial Park, Hyderabad, whose construction ran past schedule and attracted a TGIIC demand notice covering 12 November 2023 to 11 November 2025. Management says it continued to strengthen the foundations of future growth by expanding manufacturing capabilities, enhancing supply chain resilience, investing in advanced technologies and accelerating product innovation. The stated strategic expansion is to move beyond electric buses into electric trucks while building capabilities for scale and international markets, targeting production of approximately 2,500 electric vehicles by FY27. A new electric bus platform meeting evolving PM E-Drive requirements is expected to launch in Q3 FY27, and the in-house electric truck platform, built on learnings from an initial 100-truck pilot programme run through a technology partnership, is targeted for commercial launch in Q4 FY27. Heavy-duty ladder-chassis platforms under development include a 55T E-Tractor Trailer and a 35T E-Tipper, alongside in-house monocoque chassis bus platforms from 9 to 13.5 metres. In the Energy Division, 3-Cavity and 4-Cavity moulds were developed and commissioned in collaboration with machinery suppliers, increasing productivity 2 to 4 times per cycle, and the FY27 plan includes replacing old DESMA machines with VFD-driven machines. Planned FY 2026-27 facility investments at the Mobility division include VFD air compressors, solar panels for renewable power generation, an integrated power monitoring system, IoT-based energy monitoring, a bus duct extension, a dedicated power feeder line and rainwater harvesting.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Public transport electrification in India has evolved from a policy-led initiative into a structural growth opportunity, supported by government procurement programmes, improving total cost economics, expanding charging infrastructure and increasing localisation across the value chain
- India has emerged as the third-largest electric bus market globally, with domestic electric bus sales reaching 5,423 units and nearly 30% growth over the previous year
- Overall EV bus penetration in India stands at 4.7% while the strategically important 9-metre and 12-metre segments have reached nearly 9% adoption; management expects accelerated industry growth as adoption moves beyond the 10-15% threshold
- The global electric bus market grew approximately 12% year-on-year to roughly 70,000 units sold, with China accounting for nearly 60% of sales
- Composite insulators are among the fastest-growing segments of the global and Indian insulator industry, driven by increasing investments in transmission and distribution infrastructure, renewable energy integration and grid modernisation
- Composite insulators are preferred for high-voltage transmission lines in renewable energy corridors, coastal regions and challenging operating environments due to superior mechanical strength, corrosion and pollution resistance, lightweight construction and lower lifecycle maintenance cost
- Insulator division margins improved on a favourable product mix and enhanced operating leverage, with exports contributing approximately 37% of divisional revenue
- Growing demand in construction and logistics segments underpins the development of heavy-duty commercial EV platforms including a 55T E-Tractor Trailer and a 35T E-Tipper
- Management flagged geopolitical uncertainties, supply chain disruptions, battery and magnet availability challenges and global market volatility as headwinds navigated during the year
- Order Book of 10,000+ buses reported among the 2025-26 highlights
- Management states that the robust order book provides strong revenue visibility
- Strong customer relationships with State Transport Undertakings across India supported by a robust order book and strong execution capabilities
- An expanding order pipeline is cited as part of the Company's positioning for the electrification opportunity

company overview:
Olectra Greentech Limited (Hyderabad, incorporated 2000) is one of India's largest manufacturers of electric buses and a maker of composite/silicone polymer insulators. It completed homologation of its first E-Bus in 2017 and has 8+ years of e-bus manufacturing/commercialisation experience. Two reporting segments:
- **E-vehicle division** — electric buses (7m V2, 9m iX, 12m X2, Coach CX2) and electric tippers; the dominant revenue contributor.
- **Insulator division** — silicone/composite polymer insulators (higher-margin niche).

Scale markers (per deck): Market cap ~INR 102.3 bn (~USD 1.2 bn); 2,700+ EVs on Indian roads; 40+ crore (400M+) clean km; 135+ product variants; 1,000+ employees. Manufacturing at a greenfield Hyderabad plant on 150 acres acquired from TSIIC, with initial capacity 5,000 EVs/year scalable to 10,000 EVs/year.
financial health & performance:
**FY25 (consolidated, audited — from investor presentation):**
- Revenue from operations: **INR 1,80,190 lakh (~INR 1,802 cr)**, up ~56% YoY (FY24: 1,15,414 lakh).
- Adjusted EBITDA: **INR 27,632 lakh (~INR 276 cr)**, up ~49% (FY24: 18,551 lakh); EBITDA margin ~15.3% (consolidated adj.).
- PBT: INR 18,788 lakh, up ~78%; PAT: **INR 13,921 lakh (~INR 139 cr)**, up ~77% (FY24: 7,865 lakh); PAT margin ~7.7%.
- ROCE ~19.2% (FY25). Revenue CAGR FY22–FY25 ~45%; Adj. EBITDA CAGR ~106%; PAT CAGR ~58%.
- EVs sold FY25: 972 (FY24: 541).

**Segment split FY25 (12M):** E-vehicle division revenue INR 1,62,179 lakh (+60.4%), EBITDA INR 22,610 lakh (margin ~13.9%); Insulator division revenue INR 18,011 lakh (+26.0%), EBITDA INR 5,022 lakh (margin ~27.9% — the higher-margin business). Q4FY25 revenue jumped sharply (consolidated Q4 ~INR 44,892 lakh vs Q4FY24 ~28,881 lakh).

**Balance sheet (31-Mar-25, consolidated):** Total assets INR 2,17,140 lakh; Total equity INR 1,05,272 lakh. Borrowings: long-term INR 14,170 lakh (up sharply from ~918 lakh FY24, financing greenfield capex), short-term INR 11,315 lakh. Trade receivables INR 69,352 lakh (up from 51,322 — stretched, working-capital intensive). Inventories INR 28,996 lakh. CWIP INR 18,686 lakh (new plant). Cash & equivalents only INR 567 lakh plus INR 16,462 lakh other bank balances. FY25 net long-term borrowing inflow INR 13,252 lakh funded INR 17,698 lakh of PP&E/intangible capex.

**9MFY26 (per credit rating commentary):** Strong revenue growth and sustained EBITDA margins, driven by a healthy order book — the explicit basis for the rating upgrade. (No standalone 9MFY26 numbers disclosed in either source.)
e-bus delivery / order-book guidance:
- Order book **10,000+ e-buses** (deck). Cumulative orders received: cumulative grew from 90 (FY18) to a single large award of **5,150 buses** ("world's largest e-Bus order") and a peak annual order intake of 8,232 buses (FY24 bar).
- Milestones achieved: 100, 500, then 1,000 buses delivery milestones crossed; first OEM to deliver 500+ e-buses; first E-Tipper delivered.
- Capacity ramp (Hyderabad greenfield): 5,000 → 10,000 EVs/year supports delivery acceleration against the order book.
order book / tenders: Order book 10,000+ e-buses, anchored on **State Transport Undertaking (STU) tenders**. Active fleets across STUs/municipal bodies: PMPML (Pune), TGSRTC (Telangana), HRTC (Himachal), KSRTC (Kerala & Karnataka), GSRTC (Gujarat), BEST (Mumbai), MSRTC (Maharashtra), APSRTC (Andhra), NMC (Nagpur), SMC (Surat), KTCL (Goa), DSCL (Dehradun), SSCL (Silvassa), TTD (Tirumala), TMTU (Thane). Large 5,150-bus award noted as the world's largest single e-bus order.
products / portfolio: E-Bus range: V2 (7m, ~150 km), iX (9m, 180–200 km), X2 (12m, 200–300 km), CX2 Coach (~350 km); plus electric Tipper (launched 2022). Insulator division: silicone/composite polymer insulators. Expansion into electric tippers and broader EV-ecosystem/adjacent segments.
capacity / capex: Greenfield Hyderabad EV plant on 150 acres (acquired from TSIIC); initial capacity 5,000 EVs/yr scalable to 10,000 EVs/yr; operations commenced (partial) for buses and other EV products. CWIP INR 18,686 lakh at FY25-end; FY25 capex ~INR 17,698 lakh, debt-funded.
